one_sentence_story: When researchers handed elementary teachers a randomly drawn list of children disguised as 'Harvard-tested late bloomers,' young kids on that random list outgained peers because teachers unconsciously gave them warmer attention, tougher questions, and longer patience.
so_what_for_you: Treat every newcomer or struggling learner as an 'about-to-bloom' mind: give two extra seconds of wait-time after asking a question and critique mistakes as solvable puzzles rather than fixed limits.

jargon_map.plain: higher expectations eliciting stronger actual performance through subtle behavioral support
jargon_map.analogy: like watering one seedling more carefully because the packet promised prize roses

jargon_map.plain: an initially arbitrary belief causing actions that make the belief come true
jargon_map.analogy: like a rumor of a store shortage causing panic buying that actually empties the shelves

jargon_map.plain: how many seconds a teacher or manager waits silently after asking a question before moving on
jargon_map.analogy: like holding the elevator door open two extra beats so someone makes it inside

jargon_map.plain: unconscious vocal, facial, and instructional cues transmitted by someone's prior belief
jargon_map.analogy: like poker tells that give away what hand you think someone holds

jargon_map.plain: the dark mirror image where low expectations depress support and drag performance down
jargon_map.analogy: like benching a rookie at the first slip until their confidence freezes
